subject: Sales discovery: model fit & regression - pin/rollback discussion
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah O'Neill <sarah.oneill@acmeretail.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-10T15:20:00Z
Subject: Post-call recap & recommended next steps — model fit / evals

Hi Sarah — great speaking today. Quick recap from our discovery and next steps we discussed:

- Use cases: product description generation (catalog), customer support auto-summaries
- Primary constraints: low latency for read paths (<= 250ms p95), strict hallucination tolerances for catalog copy, and per-request PII redaction

Recommended model candidates (based on your prompt sets & sample corpus):
- redwood-owl-2.3 (balanced: cost/quality, strong on factuality)
- redwood-owl-3-qa (higher-quality for long-form product descriptions; higher cost)

Attached: acme_prompt_set_v2.json (prompts we used for our eval), benchmark_summary.pdf (high-level perf & quality numbers).

Immediate next steps I promised:
1) Share the evaluation artifacts (attached) and a short summary of recommended model pins/rollbacks if you see regressions after version updates.
2) If you want, we can run a runbook-style regression diff and propose a pin to a stable variant (per-route pin) so your production traffic stays safe while we explore the newer variant.
3) Schedule a follow-up to review the eval diffs and agree on rollout policy (canary %/rollback criteria).

Proposed time: Tue 4/12 10:00am PT — let me know what works.

Thanks,
Marissa
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: acme_prompt_set_v2.json (application/json)
Attachment: benchmark_summary.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Sarah O'Neill <sarah.oneill@acmeretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & recommended next steps — model fit / evals

Thanks Marissa — really helpful summary. Quick heads up: our internal team rolled the platform to redwood-owl-2.4 yesterday evening and we've started seeing a spike in hallucination-like outputs for product specs (fields like dimensions and materials are sometimes invented). This started for ~3% of requests and is visible on our QA set.

Are you able to surface a diff between 2.3 and 2.4 for the prompt sets we shared? If 2.4 is the culprit, we'd like to discuss pinning production to 2.3 until fixes are in. Procurement is copied for awareness since this could affect SLA commitments.

Appreciate any quick triage you can do.

—Sarah
Director, Product AI — Acme Retail
sarah.oneill@acmeretail.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Cc: Sarah O'Neill <sarah.oneill@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T11:00:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Re: Post-call recap & recommended next steps — model fit / evals

FYI — Acme reported a regression after an internal roll to redwood-owl-2.4. They see ~3% hallucination in product spec outputs on our shared QA prompts. They asked for a diff and asked if we can pin them to 2.3 while engineering investigates.

Key asks from customer:
- Quick diff/summary of behavioral deltas between 2.3 and 2.4 on their prompt set
- Short-term mitigation: per-route pin or rollback for production traffic (they'd prefer pinning to maintain compatibility)
- ETA for a fix or mitigation path

Can you advise on whether we can: (a) pin at the router level to redwood-owl-2.3 for Acme, (b) generate a small regression diff artifact we can share, and (c) estimate time to rollback or patch? I'm looping you to both support the ask and to give a concise recommendation to the customer.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick sync.

—Marissa

From: rishi.malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-11T12:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Post-call recap & recommended next steps — model fit / evals

Thanks for the heads up. Short answer: yes, we can support both pinning and rollback. Recommendation in order of least customer disruption:

1) Per-route pin to redwood-owl-2.3 — this is our preferred short-term mitigation. It isolates Acme's traffic without touching other tenants. We can create a route override and pin the variant for them within ~1–2 hours (including validation).

2) Canary rollback of redwood-owl-2.3 globally if the regression is widespread — we should only do this if multiple customers report the same regression.

3) If pinning is not acceptable, we can perform an immediate rollback for their dedicated pool (if they are on a dedicated plan) — requires coordination with infra and a short maintenance window.

Dev — can you confirm the steps to produce a small regression diff (run our eval harness across acme_prompt_set_v2.json against 2.3 and 2.4) and the expected artifacts (diff + CSV + example inputs/outputs)? Also please attach any preliminary diffs you can generate so we can share with the customer. I'll draft language for the pin request.

Rishi
Engineering Manager, Platform Reliability
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-12T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Post-call recap & recommended next steps — model fit / evals

All — I ran a quick eval pass overnight comparing redwood-owl-2.3 vs redwood-owl-2.4 on the acme_prompt_set_v2.json you attached. Findings (high level):

- Measured regression: increase in hallucination-like tokens from 0.8% -> 3.1% on the QA set (matches customer report)
- Primary diff: 2.4 applies a lengthening generation bias in some templates which causes extrapolation on partial spec fields; we can reproduce on a small subset of prompts

Artifacts attached: regression_diffs.txt (summary + 10 examples), eval_results_q1.csv (full per-prompt metrics). I also included a short command snippet to pin the route via our control plane APIs:

# Pin route override (example)
POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/routes/overrides
{
  "route_id": "acme/catalog-v1",
  "model_variant": "redwood-owl-2.3",
  "reason": "quality-regression-after-2.4 rollout",
  "expires_at": "2027-05-12T08:00:00Z"
}

If Marissa/Sarah approve, we can create the override and validate with a quick smoke test (10k requests sampled) and then keep it until a fix is validated. If they prefer a full rollback for their dedicated pool, that requires a short maintenance window and coordination but is doable within ~4 hours.

I've opened INF-1293 to track the regression and the remediation path (link: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/INF-1293).

Attachments: regression_diffs.txt (text/plain); eval_results_q1.csv (text/csv)

—Dev
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
